top10.introHtml: Refreshed 2026-08-07. Scanned 44 raw listings across Cars.com, CarGurus, and AutoTrader. After filtering 2-seat roadsters (Miata, S2000, Boxster, SLK, Corvette, SC430, Allante, TT Roadster, etc.) and deduplicating cross-site listings, 35 unique 4-seat convertibles in the pool. TrueCar skipped (body-style filter broken). Ranked by recency, mileage, deal rating, and make reliability.

picks.whyGood: The E93 BMW 328i is the definitive 4-seat soft-top of its era — balanced N52 inline-6, hydraulic power top with proper glass heated rear window, real usable rear seats. At 51k miles this one is barely broken in. CarGurus Good Deal badge from a franchised dealer confirms the price is honest.
picks.whatToVerify: N52 valve cover gasket and oil filter housing are known seepers at 50-80k — inspect the gasket area. Hydraulic soft-top rams: actuate a full open/close and time it — slow cycle (>25s) means low fluid or weak rams. Cooling system: thermostats and water pump on E90-era BMWs often go together at 80-100k. Check rear window de-fog function and look for water staining on rear leather.
picks.bottomLine: The benchmark 4-seat BMW convertible at genuinely low mileage — Good Deal price, proven platform, real back seats.

picks.whyGood: The B8.5 A3 Cabriolet is the most modern Audi convertible in this search — 2.0T TFSI turbocharged engine, standard MMI infotainment, folding soft top, and 4 proper seats. At 83k miles on a 2016 platform it's past the depreciation cliff but well within reliable service life. AutoTrader lists it $1,000 below the identical Cars.com listing.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm S tronic or 6-speed manual — if S tronic DSG, check for low-speed shudder under 20mph (mechatronic TSB). Full soft-top cycle open and closed — listen for binding or motor struggle. Check rear seat area for water ingress. 2.0T TFSI timing chain is belt-driven on this generation (B8.5) so less concerning than chain-tensioner models, but verify oil service records.
picks.bottomLine: Modern turbocharged convertible at a fair price — more contemporary tech than most of this list, and the A3 Cabriolet is a genuinely handsome car.

picks.whyGood: The B8 A5 Cabriolet is widely considered one of the best-looking 4-seat convertibles ever produced — long hood, sculpted flanks, and a clean roofline. At 55k miles this is low for a 2012, and the 2.0T TFSI is the most reliable engine Audi put in this body. $13,489 is fair market for a well-preserved example.
picks.whatToVerify: B8 2.0T timing chain tensioner: ask for any tensioner-related service history, or budget to inspect it — failure at high mileage is noisy but costly. Full soft-top cycle. Rear headliner and carpet for water intrusion. MMI screen and HVAC blend doors. S tronic fluid change history (Audi recommends 40k intervals but dealers often skip it).
picks.bottomLine: The prettiest car on this list at genuinely low mileage — A5 Cabriolet design has aged perfectly and 55k miles leaves a lot of driving ahead.

picks.whyGood: The newest platform in this entire search by six years. The S550 Mustang EcoBoost Premium brings independent rear suspension, modern Ford SYNC3 infotainment, and the turbocharged 2.3L EcoBoost that makes 310hp. At 132k miles it has been driven, but EcoBoost engines are genuinely robust at this range with proper maintenance. CarGurus Fair Deal — not a steal, but the 2020 premium is real.
picks.whatToVerify: Run full CARFAX at this mileage — accident history is the primary risk on a high-mileage car. S550 IRS rear cradle bushings begin showing wear at 100k+: listen for rear clunks on rough pavement. EcoBoost intercooler condensation: check for rough cold starts and misfire codes. Full power soft-top cycle. Confirm no open recalls (S550 had several safety campaigns).
picks.bottomLine: Most modern, most feature-rich Mustang in range — the right choice if you want current technology and can accept high miles on an S550 platform.

picks.whyGood: Clean title and no-accident history confirmed via Cars.com at under $10k for a 66k-mile 2013. The Chrysler 200 convertible's 2.4L Tigershark four-cylinder is uncomplicated and parts are cheap. This is the practical, no-drama choice for someone who wants a 4-seat convertible without European maintenance overhead.
picks.whatToVerify: Chrysler 200 convertibles are prone to top-latch wear — cycle the roof fully and check both front latches engage positively. Water staining under the rear seat is a common sign of past top-seal failure. Transmission: confirm automatic (200 dropped the manual mid-generation). Timing belt (not chain) on 2.4L Tigershark — check service history.
picks.bottomLine: The sensible pick — clean history, under $10k, half the maintenance cost of the European alternatives. Not exciting, but genuinely reliable.

picks.whyGood: The Murano CrossCabriolet is unlike anything else on this list — a crossover-based open-air cruiser with the VQ35DE V6 that Nissan put in everything from the 350Z to the Maxima. Good Deal badge from CarGurus. Reliable drivetrain, and the unique profile turns more heads than most conventional convertibles. Seats 4 with comfortable front chairs.
picks.whatToVerify: The CrossCabriolet's soft top is essentially structurally non-load-bearing — inspect the windshield frame and A-pillars carefully for any flex or creaking on rough roads. Top motor: cycle open and closed slowly (these motors are not fast-replaceable). Rear seat headroom is limited. VQ35 timing chain is self-tensioning and generally healthy but check for any rattle on cold start. CVT fluid change history.
picks.bottomLine: The wildcard — nothing else in this budget cruises quite like it. Buy it knowing you're choosing a conversation piece over a driver's car.

picks.whyGood: 54k miles on a 2011 Chrysler 200 is genuinely low — this car has covered only 3,000 miles per year on average. Good Deal badge, CarGurus image confirms the listing is legitimate. At $10,945 it's priced above the budget Chrysler 200s but the mileage gap justifies it.
picks.whatToVerify: Low-mileage cars that haven't been driven regularly can present their own issues: check all rubber seals and top gaskets for dry rot. Full top operation — low-mileage tops can stiffen if they haven't been exercised. Brake rotors may show surface rust from infrequent use. Confirm transmission service has been performed regardless of mileage.
picks.bottomLine: The low-mileage sleeper pick — well under average annual miles for an 11-year-old car, and priced to reflect it.

picks.whyGood: The F23 228i is the most technically advanced BMW convertible in this search — xDrive all-wheel drive, TwinPower turbocharged 2.0L (245hp), electric soft top, and active safety features absent in the E90/E93 generation. At 102k miles on the N20 engine it's well past break-in but still has significant service life ahead. AutoTrader Private Seller Exchange listing comes with their basic inspection.
picks.whatToVerify: N20 timing chain tensioner: this is the critical check for the N20 engine — cold-start rattle in the first 5 seconds indicates tensioner wear, which becomes a very expensive repair if neglected. xDrive transfer case fluid — check service history. Cooling system at 102k. Full soft-top cycle. The Private Seller Exchange inspection is not a substitute for a proper PPI at this mileage and price.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern BMW platform in this search — AWD, turbocharged, current tech — worth the premium if the N20 timing chain checks out.

picks.whyGood: Best dollar-per-car in this entire search. $7,799 for a 2014 with 87k miles, CarGurus Good Deal badge, and a proper image is the value floor. The 200 convertible at this price is straightforward to own and maintain. If the budget ceiling matters, nothing else gets you into a modern 4-seat convertible this cheaply.
picks.whatToVerify: At $7,799, the price is honest but not a windfall — inspect the top latch mechanism closely (early 200 top latches wear faster than the later 200S). Check for water in the trunk after a top cycle. Rear subframe and trailing arm bushings at this mileage. Timing belt service history on the 2.4L.
picks.bottomLine: The floor of the market — you won't find a cheaper legitimate 4-seat convertible in this area. The right buy if budget is the binding constraint.

picks.whyGood: The B8 S5 Cabriolet pairs the A5's gorgeous body with Audi's supercharged 3.0T V6 — 333hp, quattro AWD, and an exhaust note that puts the 2.0T models to shame. At 69k miles this is the performance pick of the list. Cars.com listing confirms clean title and no accidents. The supercharged V6 (CREC) is considerably more durable than the earlier B7 S4/S5's 4.2 V8.
picks.whatToVerify: Supercharger belt and tensioner: inspect for wear or slippage (service at ~80-100k recommended). Quattro drivertrain: transfer case and front differential fluid history. B8 soft-top hydraulics: full cycle test. Timing chain tensioner on the 3.0T TFSI is generally robust but verify oil records — skipped oil changes accelerate chain wear. Carbon buildup on intake valves is a known issue on direct-injection supercharged engines.
picks.bottomLine: The driver's pick — supercharged AWD performance in a beautiful Cabriolet body at a price that makes sense for what it is.

manual10.introHtml: 1 manual-transmission convertible confirmed from this refresh. Transmission data sourced from CarGurus listing metadata and Cars.com records. AutoTrader transmission data was not captured — actual manual count may be higher. Always confirm transmission before visiting.

picks.whyGood: A 4th-gen Firebird Trans Am with a manual transmission and only 33k miles is a genuine collector find — these cars covered far more than 1,200 miles per year on average during their service lives. Cars.com confirms clean title and no accidents. The LT1 5.7 V8 with the T-56 6-speed (or T-5 on V6) is the configuration worth having. This is the most viscerally American open-top driving experience in the search.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm engine and gearbox: V8 LT1 with T-56 6-speed is the desirable spec. At 32 years old and 33k miles, verify this isn't a reset odometer — request all available service history. Rust inspection is non-negotiable on a car this age: frame rails, floor pans, wheel arches, and convertible top well. Full top hydraulic system test — 4th-gen rams can weep with age. Clutch and throwout bearing condition. Check ignition switch recall completion (known 4th-gen fire risk).
picks.bottomLine: The rare find — if the odometer is genuine and the rust is clean, this is a collector-grade American V8 manual convertible at a fair price. Nothing else on this list drives like it.

mustangs.introHtml: 3 Ford Mustang convertibles (2005+, S197/S550 generation) found in range and budget. Fox-body and SN-95 (pre-2005) generations excluded. Sorted by year ascending.

picks.whyGood: The 2012 S197 V6 is the sweet spot of the Mustang lineage — the 305hp Cyclone V6 is arguably more reliable than the 4.6 V8 it replaced, returns better fuel economy, and the 2010+ refresh body is the cleanest S197 design. CarGurus Fair Deal. At 96k miles this engine has barely started.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 spring perch rust is the main structural concern — inspect both rear spring pockets carefully. Rear axle 8.8 clunk test on takeoff. Convertible top latch mechanism and hydraulic cylinders. Water staining under rear seat. Brake rotor condition at this mileage. ABS module (a known failure point on S197).
picks.bottomLine: The sensible Mustang — bulletproof V6, clean S197 facelift body, priced reasonably at 96k miles.

picks.whyGood: S550 Mustang with 141k miles is a high-mileage proposition, but the EcoBoost and Coyote V8 are both robust engines at this range when maintained. Great Deal badge from AutoTrader. The S550's independent rear suspension and modern SYNC3 cabin are a substantial upgrade over the S197.
picks.whatToVerify: Full CARFAX at 141k is essential — this many miles on a Mustang almost guarantees highway accumulation or delivery use; verify. IRS rear cradle bushings and subframe bolts at this mileage. EcoBoost intercooler condensation codes. Power top cycle. Open recall check.
picks.bottomLine: High miles on a modern platform — correct if the history is clean, but 141k warrants a thorough PPI before committing.

picks.whyGood: Newest Mustang in the search with the most modern platform. 2020 S550 brings all the S550 refinements plus the most recent suspension tuning. EcoBoost Premium means premium interior, active exhaust optional, and SYNC3 with Apple CarPlay. CarGurus Fair Deal at $14,995 — 2020 Mustang convertibles hold value.
picks.whatToVerify: Same S550 checklist: CARFAX first, IRS bushing inspection, EcoBoost cold-start behavior, power top, open recalls. Confirm EcoBoost vs GT V8 — listing badge may be ambiguous. At $14,995 this is the top of the budget, so negotiate against CarGurus pricing data.
picks.bottomLine: Most modern Mustang convertible available in range — buy it if the history is clean and you want the freshest S550 at the budget ceiling.
